evals.prompt: can you review evals/files/order_processor.py? i inherited it from someone and want to know whats wrong with it design-wise before i add a 'platinum' customer tier and a PDF report
evals.expected_output: A structured review ordered by severity flagging SRP (god class), OCP (customer_type and fmt switches), DIP (hard-coded sqlite/smtp/clock), SQL injection, hard-coded credentials, swallowed exception, magic numbers, -1 sentinel; with concrete fix sketches and an offer to refactor.
assertions: Flags the class as having too many responsibilities (SRP / god class)
Flags the customer_type if/elif chain as the reason adding 'platinum' is painful (OCP), with a fix
Flags the fmt if/elif in report() as the reason adding PDF is painful (OCP), with a fix
Flags hard-coded sqlite/SMTP/datetime.now dependencies as hurting testability (DIP / injection)
Flags the SQL injection from string concatenation
Flags the hard-coded SMTP credentials
Flags the bare except: pass that swallows DB errors
Flags magic numbers (0.8, 0.9, 0.5, 1.2) and/or the -1 error sentinel
Findings are ordered or labeled by severity
Includes concrete fix code sketch(es)

evals.prompt: I need a TypeScript notification service for our backend. It should send a message to a user via email, SMS, or Slack depending on their preference, retry up to 3 times on failure, and log each attempt. We'll probably add push notifications and WhatsApp later. Write the code.
evals.expected_output: TypeScript code with a channel abstraction, a channel registry so new channels are added without modifying the service, injected dependencies (logger, channels, possibly sleep/clock), retry logic separated from sending, and brief design notes.
assertions: Defines a channel abstraction (interface/type) implemented separately per channel
Adding a new channel (push/WhatsApp) does not require editing the core service's logic (registry/map, not a switch)
Dependencies (logger, channels) are injected rather than constructed inside the service
Retry logic is separated from channel-specific sending code
Retries up to 3 attempts and logs each attempt
Handles the case of an unknown/unregistered channel preference explicitly
Includes brief design notes explaining the structure

evals.prompt: quick python script pls: rename every .jpeg file in a folder (passed as cli arg) to .jpg. just a one-off thing for my photos
evals.expected_output: A short, simple script without unnecessary classes, interfaces, or DI; still uses clear names, pathlib, and handles basic errors (missing dir, name collisions).
assertions: Script is short (under ~60 lines of code) with no classes/interfaces/DI
Takes the folder as a CLI argument
Handles a missing/invalid directory with a clear error
Avoids overwriting an existing .jpg on name collision
Uses clear names (no cryptic one-letter variables beyond loop idioms)
